heart_basics: The heart pumps blood through the body. Arteries carry blood away from the heart, while veins return blood to it. For personal concerns, ask a qualified healthcare professional.
heart_risk: Factors associated with cardiovascular risk include elevated blood pressure, high cholesterol, tobacco exposure, family history and some health conditions. A clinician can assess your individual risk.
heart_food: A heart-supportive eating pattern can include vegetables, fruits, whole grains, beans, and unsaturated fats, with attention to excess sodium. A clinician or dietitian can tailor advice.
heart_activity: Regular enjoyable movement, such as walking or cycling, can support cardiovascular health. Choose activity suited to your abilities and ask a healthcare professional about any medical restrictions.
heart_prevention: General heart-supportive habits include sufficient sleep, varied nutritious food, movement, avoiding tobacco, and recommended healthcare visits.
heart_screening: Blood pressure and cholesterol are commonly checked as part of cardiovascular risk assessment. Ask a healthcare professional which checks and timing are right for you.
heart_symptoms: New, unusual, persistent, or concerning symptoms should be assessed by a healthcare professional. Sudden or severe symptoms may need emergency medical services.
heart_recovery: Following a clinician-provided care plan, attending follow-up visits, and discussing cardiac rehabilitation when appropriate can support recovery. Do not change prescribed medicines without a clinician.
